text:
incident-bot: PAGER: GPU pool 'livemux-prod-gpu' queue depth rising rapidly (>90% sustained for 4m). Autoscaler attempts failing. Paging @oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: Seeing alerts, joining. what's the primary symptom?

incident-bot: Symptoms: queue growth, API 429s on generation endpoints, increased token latency. Autoscale requests sent but no new VMs registered for 3 consecutive attempts. Recent kernel/driver errors surfaced on several nodes.

ashwin: I'm on it. quick check: how many nodes are in pool?

maya: pool size: desired 64, active 51, queued requests 12k. autoscaler logs: target instances requested but provisioning timed out. kube nodes show flapping on 3 hosts (compute-34/35/36).

kevin: I can pull driver logs, looks like repeated CUDA Xid 13 on compute-35 around 02:11:03. also OOM messages from runtime: "tensorflow: cudnn allocation failed" then node lost readiness.

elaine: If nodes are losing GPU capacity due to driver faults, autoscaler will request more but they never become healthy -> effective capacity drop. Suggest immediate mitigations: 1) pause new low-priority batch jobs 2) temporarily increase max scale if cloud has spare quota 3) cordon flapping nodes and drain safely.

ashwin: Agreed. Oncall: can you run the playbook step: "mitigate-gpu-pool-surge"?

oncall-sre: Running now. Step 1: apply ingress throttle for /v1/generate for accounts with <500 monthly calls.

maya: Throttle rule applied via CDN edge config. Dropped ~30% incoming rate within 30s. Monitoring queue.

kevin: Starting targeted cordon/drain of compute-35. Command: ```kubectl cordon compute-35 && kubectl drain compute-35 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60```

deploy-bot: Deploy event: scaling policy tweak applied (max pool increased from 80 -> 96) by ashwin. No new instances registered yet.

ops-bot: Cloud provider returned rate limit on instance create for 90s, then provisioning retries resumed.

elaine: If cloud create is rate-limited, scale bump won't help immediately. Need to recover existing nodes or fallback to model-variant routing to smaller models to reduce per-request GPU usage.

ashwin: Can we route low-latency customers to smaller-quantized model variants?

maya: Yes, can push a routing policy: route requests tagged "cost-sensitive" to rdx-small-quant. Preparing rollout.

kevin: Drain of compute-35 started. Logs show repeated driver_restart sequence: ```nvidia: probe failed, Xid 13, gpu reset required``` then node kubelet marks NotReady. We're seeing kernel NV driver re-init loops.

ashwin: OK salvage attempt: try to remote-restart driver on node first to avoid full reboot. Command: ```sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver-monitor || sudo modprobe -r nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia``` execute with caution.

kevin: Ran remote driver restart on compute-35, returned Xid count still climbing. Reboot scheduled. Rebooting node.

oncall-sre: Reboot initiated for compute-35. ETA to rejoin ~6m.

incident-bot: Customer impact summary (preliminary): 6 customers experiencing elevated latency, 2 customers seeing transient 429s. Error budget burn increasing. Incident severity: P2->escalating because sustained degradation.

elaine: Notify support to open CS tickets for affected customers (include timeframe, mitigations).

ashwin: Support notified. Template posted in #support: "We're investigating a GPU pool capacity issue affecting generation latency. Mitigations: throttles, routing to quantized models, cordon/drain of unstable nodes. ETA initial recovery: ~15m."

maya: compute-35 rebooted and rejoined cluster but kubelet reports GPU not ready: driver module present but cuda init fails with Xid 37 now.

kevin: Moving to drain compute-36 next. Reboot compute-35 again if needed. Also starting kernel message snapshot: ```dmesg | tail -n 200``` attached in logs (link).

oncall-sre: While you do that, I'm enabling routing fallback: route 40% of traffic to rdx-small-quant for all non-enterprise customers. That cut queue by ~45% within 2m.

incident-bot: Autoscaler: attempts=12, successes=0 in last 6m, cloud quota remaining=14 instances.

elaine: With quota available but provisioning failures and driver instability, safest path is combination: route more traffic off GPUs + recover nodes. Please avoid bulk reboots until we isolate root cause.

kevin: I dumped kernel logs from compute-36: pattern looks like temperature spike -> driver reset -> Xid timeout -> GPU lost. Could be power/thermals. Metrics show GPU temp hopped to 92C before resets.

maya: Thermal alerts correlate with older firmware on compute-36/35. Both are running driver v470 with mixed firmware. We recently pushed a model variant with longer sequence lengths causing sustained full utilization.

ashwin: Hypothesis: workload shift -> sustained peak utilization -> thermal stress -> driver resets -> node flapping -> autoscaler retries -> queue growth. Plan: 1) route load to smaller models 2) reduce bin-packing of long-seq jobs 3) schedule rolling maintenance for old firmware nodes 4) set emergency autoscaler backoff to prevent futile create attempts.

oncall-sre: Implementing plan items 1 & 4 now. Backoff set to 10m between provisioning retries.

ops-bot: Cloud provider now successfully provisioned 6 new nodes; 4 registered healthy. Effective capacity +4 GPUs. Queue down 30%.

incident-bot: Timeline update: 02:11 pager fired -> 02:12 throttles applied -> 02:16 routing fallback -> 02:20 compute-35 reboot -> 02:24 compute-35 rejoin attempt failed -> 02:30 compute-36 drained -> 02:34 4 new nodes joined -> 02:42 queue trending down, 429s reduced.

maya: Recommending follow-up action items for postmortem: - firmware audit for fleet - workload backpressure policies for long sequences - autoscaler smarter failure handling - emergency model routing playbook documented.

ashwin: Agree. Oncall handoff: I'm taking the incident for the next 2h to watch for reoccurrence, will coordinate with infra to schedule firmware updates.

elaine: I'll own the customer comms and postmortem draft. Please add logs/metrics snapshots to the ticket.

kevin: Adding GPU thermal telemetry and driver traces to incident folder. Link sent in thread.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigation in place, partial recovery. Paging suppressed. Further updates in this thread. :white_check_mark:
